title: Ukraine's new drone blitz cuts Russian oil refining capacity by 30 percent
gist: After pausing in October under US pressure over global fuel prices, Ukraine resumed long-range drone strikes on October 30 and hit nine of Russia's thirty-five major refineries in ten days, cutting refining capacity by around 30% (Reuters) and triggering petrol rationing in several Russian regions. Dickinson frames Ukraine's 3,000km strike capability as both war leverage and its real security guarantee, with Russia's size now a liability.

insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Concentrated refinery outages tighten Russian product exports (diesel/gasoline) and support crack spreads.

insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: A ~30% refining hit implies more Russian crude pushed to export and fewer product exports — watch diesel cracks and Urals flows.

insights.so_what: US political sensitivity to fuel prices acts as a brake on Ukraine's strike campaign — a key swing factor for oil price risk.

themes.theme: Long-range strike as leverage and deterrent

insights.claim: Ukrainian long-range drones can now hit high-value targets up to three thousand kilometers away, versus only very basic long-range systems in 2022.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Strike reach covers most of European Russia's energy infrastructure — few Russian assets are out of range.
